## SECTION I General Provisions Applying to Both Fast Track and Intermediate Track

## Scope of this Part

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Scope of this Part] 28.1 .  This section contains general provisions about the management of cases allocated to the fast and intermediate tracks. Section II contains further provisions about the management of cases allocated to the fast track, other than for cases of noise induced hearing loss. Section III contains provisions about the management of noise induced hearing loss cases allocated to the fast track. Section IV contains further provisions about the management of cases allocated to the intermediate track.

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Scope of this Part] (Part 27 sets out the procedure for claims allocated to the small claims track.)

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Scope of this Part] (Part 29 sets out the procedure for claims allocated to the multi-track.)

## General provisions

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > General provisions] 28.2. —(1) The court shall give directions for the management of the case and set a timetable for the steps to be taken between the giving of the directions and the trial.

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > General provisions] 2) When it allocates a case to the fast track, the court shall give directions unless it considers that it is necessary to fix a case management conference.

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > General provisions] (3) When it allocates a case to the intermediate track, the court may give directions or fix a case management conference under rule 28.12.

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > General provisions] (4) When it gives directions, the court shall—

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > General provisions] (a)make an order in relation to disclosure; and

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > General provisions] (b)either—

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > General provisions] (i)fix the trial date; or

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > General provisions] (ii)fix a period, not exceeding 3 weeks, within which the trial is to take place.

## Variation of case management timetable

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Variation of case management timetable] 28.3. —(1) A party must apply to the court if they wish to vary any date which the court has fixed for—

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Variation of case management timetable] (a)any case management conference;

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Variation of case management timetable] (b)any pre-trial review;

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Variation of case management timetable] (c)filing the pre-trial check list;

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Variation of case management timetable] (d)the trial; or

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Variation of case management timetable] (e)the trial period.

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Variation of case management timetable] (2) Any date set by the court or these Rules for doing any act may not be varied by the parties if the variation would make it necessary to vary any of the dates mentioned in paragraph (1).

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Variation of case management timetable] (Rule 2.11 allows the parties to vary a date by written agreement except where the rules provide otherwise or the court orders otherwise.)

## Pre-trial check list (listing questionnaire)

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Pre-trial check list (listing questionnaire)] 28.4. —(1) The court shall send the parties a pre-trial check list (listing questionnaire) for completion and return by the date specified in the notice of allocation unless it considers that the claim can proceed to trial without the need for a pre-trial check list.

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Pre-trial check list (listing questionnaire)] (2) The date specified for filing a pre-trial check list shall not be more than 8 weeks before the trial date or the beginning of the trial period.

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Pre-trial check list (listing questionnaire)] (3) If no party files the completed pre-trial check list by the date specified, the court shall order that unless a completed pre-trial check list is filed within 7 days from service of that order, the claim, defence and any counterclaim shall be struck out without further order of the court.

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Pre-trial check list (listing questionnaire)] (4) If—

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Pre-trial check list (listing questionnaire)] (a)a party files a completed pre-trial check list but another party does not;

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Pre-trial check list (listing questionnaire)] (b)a party has failed to give all the information requested by the pre-trial check list; or

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Pre-trial check list (listing questionnaire)] (c)the court considers that a hearing is necessary to enable it to decide what directions to give in order to complete preparation of the case for trial, the court may give such directions as it thinks appropriate.

## Fixing or confirming the trial date and giving directions

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Fixing or confirming the trial date and giving directions] 28.5. —(1) As soon as practicable after the date specified for filing a completed pre-trial check list the court shall—

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Fixing or confirming the trial date and giving directions] (a)fix the date for the trial, unless it has already done so;

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Fixing or confirming the trial date and giving directions] (b)give any directions for the trial, including a trial timetable, which it considers appropriate; and

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Fixing or confirming the trial date and giving directions] (c)specify any further steps that need to be taken before trial.

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Fixing or confirming the trial date and giving directions] (2) The court shall give the parties at least 3 weeks’ notice of the date of the trial unless, in exceptional circumstances, the court directs that shorter notice be given.

## Conduct of trial

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Conduct of trial] 28.6. Unless the trial judge otherwise directs, the trial shall be conducted in accordance with any order previously made.

## SECTION II Provisions Applying Only to Cases Allocated to the Fast Track

## Directions

## 28.7. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.7. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (a)disclosure of documents;

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.7. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (b)service of witness statements;

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.7. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (c)expert evidence; and

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.7. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (d)whether to order or encourage the parties to engage in alternative dispute resolution.

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.7. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (Rule 26.9(6) deals with limitations in relation to expert evidence and the likely length of trial in fast track cases.)

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.7. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (2) Directions to be given under rule 28.2(1) shall be in the form set out at http://www.justice.gov.uk/courts/procedure-rules/civil, unless the court orders otherwise.

## Costs

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Costs] 28.8. The court’s power to award costs is limited in accordance with Section VI and Section IX of Part 45.

## Directions

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Directions] 28.9. Directions to be given under rule 28.2(1) shall be in the form set out at http://www.justice.gov.uk/courts/procedure-rules/civil, unless the court orders otherwise.

## Limitation

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Limitation] 28.10. —(1) The court may order a preliminary trial on limitation if satisfied that it is necessary in the interests of justice to do so.

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Limitation] (2) If any party seeks a direction for a preliminary trial on limitation, this must be identified in that party’s directions questionnaire.

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Limitation] (3) Where a preliminary trial on limitation is ordered in respect of one or more, but not all, defendants, the claims against all the other defendants shall be stayed until determination of the preliminary issue.

## Costs

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Costs] 28.11 .  The court’s power to award costs is limited in accordance with Section VIII and Section IX of Part 45.

## SECTION IV Provisions Applying Only to Cases Allocated to the Intermediate Track

## Case management conference

## 28.12. The court may fix a case management conference and may fix a pre-trial review.

## Agreement of directions

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Agreement of directions] 28.13 .  The parties must endeavour to agree appropriate directions for the management of the proceedings and submit agreed directions, or their respective proposals to the court at least seven days before any case management conference. Where the court approves agreed directions, or issues its own directions, the parties shall be so notified by the court and the case management conference will be vacated accordingly.

## Directions

## 28.14. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.14. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (a)disclosure of documents;

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.14. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (b)service of witness statements;

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.14. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (c)expert evidence;

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.14. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (d)whether to fix a pre-trial review;

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.14. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (e)listing the case for trial; and

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.14. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (f)whether to order or encourage the parties to engage in alternative dispute resolution.

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.14. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (2) The following provisions apply in respect of directions in the intermediate track—

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.14. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (a)oral expert evidence is limited to one witness per party, save where the oral evidence of a second expert for any party is reasonably required and is proportionate; and

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.14. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (b)the trial time estimate must not exceed 3 days.

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.14. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (3) The following provisions apply in respect of directions in the intermediate track, unless the court orders otherwise—

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.14. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (a)Omitted

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.14. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (b)the total length of all the permitted witness statements and witness summaries of a party shall not exceed 30 pages; and

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.14. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (c)any expert report shall not exceed 20 pages—

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.14. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (i)including the expert’s description of the issues on which they are instructed to give their opinion, the conclusions they have reached and the reasons for those conclusions; but

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > 28.14. —(1) The matters to be dealt with by directions under rule 28.2(1) include—] (ii)excluding the expert’s curriculum vitae, any supporting materials to which the reasons for their conclusions refer and any necessary photographs, plans and academic articles attached to the report.

## Costs

[PART 28 – THE FAST TRACK AND THE INTERMEDIATE TRACK > Costs] 28.15. The court’s power to award costs is limited in accordance with Section VII and Section IX of Part 45.
